thread.title: Apple’s stock tumble pushed market cap below $700 billion for first time since February 2017

author: kopitiambot.com
title: Apple’s stock tumble pushed market cap below $700 billion for first time since February 2017
text:
(Source: marketwatch.com )
Shares of Apple Inc.
AAPL, -2.59%
sank 2.6% in Monday’s abbreviated session to close at the lowest level since July 12, 2017, amid a broad-market selloff . The decline has pushed the technology giant’s market capitalization below the $700 billion mark for the first time since Feb. 10, 2017, according to FactSet data. Apple’s stock has now plunged 36.7% since it the Oct. 3, 2018 record close of $232.07, with the market cap plummeting about $404.5 billion from its peak of about $1.10 trillion. The stock’s price decline during that time has shaved about 578 points off the Dow Jones Industrial Average’s
DJIA, -2.91%
price, or about 11.5% of the Dow’s 5,036-point drop during that time. Apple is currently the second-largest use company by market cap, behind first-place Microsoft Corp.
MSFT, -4.17%
at $722.7 billion and just ahead of Google parent Alphabet Inc.
GOOGL, -0.66%
at about $684.8 billion, according to FactSet. Amazon.com Inc.
AMZN, -2.43%
is in fourth place at $657.2 billion.
